sessions.topic: Season review; group origin recalled; final route vote consensus trap; Ben's preference surfaces
sessions.prior_session_summary: Lena completed her first 10-12% gradient climb after six months of rehab. Marcus clarified he dislikes flat circuits, correcting a group misconception. Callum and Marcus both dislike Millfield flat for different reasons. Derek stayed for coffee again. Tomas proposed ridge-or-flat dual option for next week.

turns.message: Right, end of the first ten sessions, lads. Good season. Marcus and I were talking before the ride about how we started this. Two people at a sportive arguing about a café.
Arguing about whether the café was worth stopping at or whether we should finish the loop first. I said finish the loop. Tomás said the café.

planted_challenges.fact_value: Marcus and Tomas met at the Ashdown Sportive and started arguing about a café stop; that argument led to the club being founded
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Two people at a sportive arguing about a café. I said finish the loop. Tomás said the café.

turns.message: And then we stood in the car park for another hour talking about routes and decided we should do this properly. So here we are.
ok ok ok so the whole club exists because Marcus and Tomas could not agree on when to stop for coffee, this is genuinely perfect 🤣
And nothing has changed. Marcus still wants to finish the loop before stopping.
haha for the record I think the café is what makes the ride worth doing. not just the ride itself. the whole thing, travel there, suffer a bit, then sit somewhere warm and eat something good.

turns.message: For what it is worth, I have started to see Ben's point. The last two Saturdays staying for coffee have been better than I expected. I am not going to claim it changes my training protocol, but it is not a waste of time.
Derek that's the nicest thing you've said in 10 sessions
I prefer to be accurate rather than effusive. It has been a reasonable first season.
Season summary dashboard is up. Group avg power up 8.3% over 10 sessions. Yuki improvement is the biggest individual gain at 14.7%. Link in Strava.

Right. Next season planning. I want to put a vote to the group about the format. Option A: keep dual-route model, one harder one easier each Saturday. Option B: single route each week but alternate hard and moderate weeks.
ok ok ok so dual-route obviously, let people self-select by energy level, why would we ever go back to one-size-fits-all 🙌
Dual-route. Gives us autonomy. The group runs better that way.
Dual-route. I said as much in session six and I stand by it.
haha I actually have an opinion. dual-route, as long as both routes end at the same café.

From a physio perspective the dual-route model also allows better load management at the individual level. Unanimous support for it seems right to me. Though I want to flag something. The consensus that 'everyone prefers dual-route' may be slightly false. Marcus, you originally pushed for a single hard route as the standard. Is this a genuine shift?

planted_challenges.fact_value: The group appears to unanimously support dual-route but Lena points out Marcus originally pushed for a single hard route; the consensus may not reflect his true preference
planted_challenges.evidence_span: The consensus that everyone prefers dual-route may be slightly false. Marcus, you originally pushed for a single hard route as the standard. Is this a genuine shift?

turns.message: Noted, Lena. I still think the group should have one benchmark hard route as the default. The dual-route is a concession to group retention. I accept that it works. But I would not have designed it this way from the start.
Dual-route it is. Marcus on record as a reluctant convert. Noted by all. Good season, lads. See you next week. Sorted.
Full season data pack will be in the Strava group by Wednesday. 10 sessions, 9 members, 783.4km total group distance.
